summary:
I wrote plan.md for a row of ten low historic Army buildings in white and cream with green trim, using grey and red roofs. The roofs are only planned, not dry-run with the roof tool. Each irregular footprint is a gabled or hipped main block plus low lean-tos on the leftover cells; on the angled plots the ridges step south-east along the diagonal.
It reads as the Presidio through the stepped grey warehouse with green sliding doors and a GYM sign, the cream Mission building (red hip roof, arched arcade), the white porch house and the 1915 Coast Guard station with its glass cupola and US flag. Ten Presidio buildings, each on its footprint in site orientation: white/cream walls on a plinth, red or grey roofs with lean-tos, green trim and shutters, a flagpole and cupola on the Coast Guard station, with lawns and lamps.
Elements checklist and palette are in elements.md and plan.md. Interiors are hollow, lit volumes (exterior-only kit).
Six parts: two shell parts, two roof parts, facade fittings, grounds and light.

shells plots 0-3: parts/shell-a.mjs builds the walls for plots 0-3 on the plan's masses. Hall, admin and storehouse masses use one perimeter wall per building, so there is no partition where sections touch. make.sh produced a whole build.nbt and `mcd check` shows no floating blocks.
polish: Render tiles were not inspected by eye; the part was only checked with `mcd check`.
fit and the plan.md/elements.md ticks were not done.
The arcade piers (x39, 42, 45, 46 at z2 and z3, y1..2) are placed here; the upside-down stair arches at y3 are left to the fittings part.
The y3 decks are birch_planks inside the wall perimeter, so the y3 string course (cut_sandstone on plot 1, quartz on plot 2) sits at deck level.
Window and door openings are not yet cut: the walls are solid, so the fittings part must cut them.

waste.what: Wrote a local unionWalls helper, because wallBox on touching masses leaves partition walls where they meet and cannot take a string course.
waste.cost: 1 helper, about 15 lines
waste.tool: A wallUnion(g, rects, y0, y1, mat, plinth, string) helper in vocab, or a wallBox option for several rects.

companions.task: Quoins and plinth variation (cracked or mossy stone_bricks near the ground and corners) on the finished walls.

summary:
shells plots 4-9: parts/shell-b.mjs builds the walls, stone-brick plinths and y3 birch decks for plots 4-9 (office O, bike shop S, coast guard C/C1/C2/C3/C4, OCC cross, garage G/G1-G4, boathouse B/B1 and lean-tos), 874 blocks, no REFUSED or off-palette writes.
Every OPENINGS cell for plots 4-9 is left as air, and plot 4's corner quoins are in the shell. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; `mcd check` reports no floating or unsupported blocks, and close-up renders of plots 6 and 8 read as their masses.
Plan.md Notes records the shell and the OCC union helper; elements.md is not ticked because its shell and deck items are shared with part 1.
polish: elements.md: the shell item (P1 plots 0-3 and P2 plots 4-9) and the upper-floor deck item (plots 1, 2 are part 1's) stay unticked, since they are shared; my plots are done.
No mason detail beyond the plot 4 quoins: no sills, lintels, string courses, mossy/cracked variation, or plot 5 shopfront plinth (the shopfront cut removes the y1 course under the glass, by design).
Roofs and lean-to roofs (C3, C4, G1-G4, B lean-tos, S slab, cupola base) belong to roofs-b and are not built here; the wall tops at y4/y3/y2 are where those roofs start.
Fittings must place glass, doors and shutters into the air cells I carved; any OPENINGS cell not carved is a wall the fittings cannot open.

waste.what: Carved each OPENINGS cell one by one with carve(g, [x,y,z], [x,y,z]) across plots 4-9, about 60 calls worked out from the table by hand.
waste.cost: about 60 carve calls and 15 min of hand coordinate work per plot group
waste.tool: A helper openings(g, OPENINGS_ROWS) that takes the plan's OPENINGS table (plot, face, cell ranges) and carves them, or a shared wallRects/wallUnion helper so the cross plans and the openings come from the same table.

waste.what: Wrote a local unionWalls helper for the OCC cross plan (perimeter by neighbour test) because wallBox only takes a rect and two overlapping rects would put walls inside the other arm.
waste.cost: one helper, about 25 lines, one retry on the deck-interior logic
waste.tool: vocab wallBox that accepts a list of rects (a union footprint) and returns its interior cells, so every L or cross plan (plots 1, 3, 6, 7, 8) gets it without a local copy.

waste.what: Checked the four corners of the office and the boathouse door by reading the zoomed renders; I did not measure the cell counts against the plan's footprints by a tool.
waste.cost: 2 zoom renders and eyeballing
waste.tool: mcd fit or a footprint check that compares built wall cells against the plan's # maps per plot.

companions.task: Quoins, sills and lintels on the office and coast guard, and the alternating long and short quoins at each corner, plus a mossy/cracked variant at under one in ten blocks near the ground.
The shopfront glass band on the bike shop and the coast guard's four-pane y4 window, with the transom at x112..113 y3, so the openings I carved are filled to the plan.
Eave and floor lanterns in the carved porch and shopfront bays, so the shells stay lit without spawns.

summary:
roofs plots 0-3: roof.json lays W3 (grey gable, the first roof, after the shell); parts/roofs-a.mjs reroofs W1, W2, W4 (grey), A, A1 (red hips), H (grey gable), L1-L3 (red gables), then the hand lean-tos, vestibule deck, A2 arcade shed, back stoop, porch and rear sheds.
make.sh runs to a whole build.nbt with the part in it, but the roofs-a line still shows 46 REFUSED writes (A1 eave, lean-to/W3 junction) and the vestibule deck reports as floating.
Not done: trusses (none in roof.json), no render or look at the tiles, plan.md not ticked; only the W1-W4 roof item is ticked in elements.md.
polish: 46 REFUSED writes in the roofs-a line: 'A1 eave' cells at x46..53 z1..4 y3..4 (brick stairs/slabs of A1 and A's north eave) and 1 cell where W2's gable verge meets the W2 north wall (18,5,12). Clearing them needs A1's footprint/overhang reworked against A's eave; not resolved.

Vestibule deck (x12..15 z0..1 at y5, quartz_slab coping on z0, smooth_stone_slab on z1) is reported FLOATING by $MCD check: it sits on the plot-0 vestibule walls at y4, so the shell's top course there needs checking (shell-a wallBox 12,0,15,1 y1..4).

Porch roof (H1, via porch()): polished_andesite_slab at y4 over the y3 bottom slabs is reported 'on a bottom slab' by $MCD fit (x69..72 z1); the porch shed's z1 course needs top slabs or a different stacking.
Orphan slabs at 46,4,1 and 53,4,1 (A1 eave brick_slab) and orphan slabs at 6,5,14 / 23,5,14 / 13,9,14 / 16,9,14 (W2/W3 valley and ridge slabs) from $MCD check.
W3 roof has no trusses: roof.json lacks a 'trusses' block (add "trusses": {"material": "stripped_dark_oak_log"} once the hall is reviewed; W3 is an 8 x 22 span).
Warnings still open: W3 and W4 'big plane' (24-cell unbroken slope) and 'single flat expanse' (2 tones); add a dormer, monitor or cross-gable, or a third tone.
Lean-tos a..k at y4 and the back stoop/A2 sheds have not been looked at in a render; the lean-to d (x4..7 z16..17) was left in place and its stairs sit under W3's north eave.
Render not done: no `$MCD render` tiles were looked at, so the roof silhouette and the gable reads are unverified.
A2 arcade roof placed at y4 (over the arch course at y3), not y3 as the plan's ROOFS table says: the arches are at y3, so a y3 roof would collide with them.

waste.what: Bisecting the REFUSED writes by hand: disabling blocks of roofs-a one at a time, copying the file, rebuilding, restoring it, to find which roof or lean-to wrote into which neighbour's cells.
waste.cost: about 8 build runs and 6 file edits; roughly 10 minutes of the 12-minute window
waste.tool: A per-call refusal report from runParts (the reroof/leanTo call that refused, with its footprint) would have located each clash directly; the parts-report.json needs a 'refused by call' breakdown.

waste.what: Finding out, by trial, the roof.json material and trim names that keep the palette: 'bricks' and 'stone_brick' autoMix to granite, mossy_cobblestone and andesite slabs, all off-palette; a mix object is taken verbatim.
waste.cost: about 6 dry-run and make cycles, each with a palette fix
waste.tool: roof-texture's autoMix should respect the palette (or the roof doc should say a single block is expanded by autoMix); a palette-aware mode for `$MCD roof --dry-run` would catch it at once.

waste.what: Working out per-mass overhang sides ({N,S,E,W}) by hand so that neighbouring roofs do not overlap (W2 south vs W3 north, W4 north vs W3 south, A1 vs A's north eave).
waste.cost: about 6 edits and 4 builds
waste.tool: A `$MCD roof --detect-clash` (or runParts overlap warning per roof footprint) that lists which overhang sides collide with a neighbour's roof cells before any write.

waste.what: Checking the roof spec's key names (fascia, soffit, verge, ridge, gable, overhang sides) by reading roofs.mjs source.
waste.cost: 3 greps and reads of roofs.mjs lines 230-300
waste.tool: The toolkit reference (references/toolkit.md) should list the roof spec keys, their accepted values and defaults, as `$MCD roof --spec` takes them.

waste.what: Writing 11 leanTo/porch calls and 9 roof calls one by one, each with a hand-copied rect and dir.
waste.cost: one generator file, about 40 lines; fine but repetitive
waste.tool: A `lean-tos from the plan table` helper that reads plan.md's lean-to table (rect, dir, y) and calls leanTo for each row.

companions.task: Check the grey and red roof courses at the eaves and the hip valleys (A's T-join with A3, W2 into W3's valley) and fix the stair and slab courses where they meet the gable verges.
Brace W3 (8 x 22 span) and W4 with the trusses block once the walls are settled: pick king post or Fink, set the tie and purlins, and check the frame sits inside the loft.
Lay the lean-to courses (a..k) and the A2 arcade shed so their stairs face the hall and the headroom stays clear of the W3 eave, without the clearing writes that cause the refusals.

summary: roofs plots 4-9 and cupola: ["parts/roofs-b.mjs builds the red roofs O, S, C (main hip), C1 gable with quartz pediment, OCC cross hip, G, B, B1, the lean-tos of plots 5, 6, 8, 9 and the bike-shop side bay slab, then cupola([125,6], 7).", "make.sh runs clean for this part: 847 blocks placed, no OFF-PALETTE, no REFUSED; render shows red roofs and the cupola on the coast guard station.", "Roofs are laid in build() through the roof library's roof() with an explicit brick mix; roof.json is not used, and no truss frames were added."]
polish: Cosmetic: check reports 10 ORPHAN brick_slab on the S and B gable verges and fascia (they sit one cell out from the walls, by design); not fixed.
Floating: while shells 4-9 are stubs, the white_concrete gables and roofs of S, G and B float in the check; this clears when shell-b lands.
Not run: `$MCD roof --dry-run` and the roof.json spec, so no trusses were framed; the roofs were laid by roof() in build(), not from roof.json.
The lean-to sheds of plots 0-3 and the Lean-to sheds checklist item in elements.md are not complete from this part (only plots 5, 6, 8, 9 are done).
The fascia uses bricks, the soffit bricks, and the trim quartz_block; a palette-clean finish for the verges still needs confirming on the real shells.

waste.what: Found which roof wrote stray cells by hand: wrapping g.set and probe scripts in /tmp, one per roof, to see which call placed each slab.
waste.cost: about 4 probe runs and 3 rebuilds
waste.tool: runParts report that names the roof call (or the cell owner) for every block a roof writes outside its footprint

waste.what: Tried roof material names one at a time (red-tile, bricks, explicit mix) until the palette check was clean; red-tile's mix adds granite, mangrove and mud-brick stairs and slabs that are off palette.
waste.cost: 5 rebuilds
waste.tool: A roof material check that lists, before writing, which stairs and slabs a named palette or mix would produce, with a palette-safe mix suggestion

waste.what: Worked out the lean-tos and slab roofs cell by cell (direction, rect, y, edge block) for each shed.
waste.cost: about 12 leanTo/slab calls written by hand
waste.tool: A roof spec that takes lean-tos as a list of rects with dir and stair material, so the hand part reduces to one table

waste.what: Used the 45-degree and pitch values from plan.md without the roof spec check, so no --dry-run run was made.
waste.cost: 0 retries, but no dry-run warnings were checked
waste.tool: `mcd roof ... --spec roof.json --dry-run` on the roof-b rects as a separate spec file

companions.task: The verge (barge) boards and fascia on the shop and garage gables, so the rakes read as roof edges and not as stray cells; they would also set the eave flashing by hand.
The lean-to courses of C3, C4, G1, G2, G3, B west and south: stairs facing up the slope with the edge course set, so the sheds meet the walls cleanly.

summary:
facade fittings: parts/fittings.mjs places every OPENINGS window, tall window, door pair, sliding door and shutter for plots 0-9, plus the arcade arches, the bike-shop awning and BIKES banners, and the flag at x120 z1.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt: the facade fittings line shows 408 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Fit lists 25 floating shutters, all on plots 4 and 6, whose walls shell-b has not built yet.
Not done: the GYM sign (its fascia cells are locked wall) and the quartz jambs (locked wall cells, so jambs: false / frame: false); both are logged in plan.md Notes.
polish: GYM sign not placed: the z0 fascia cells x12..14 y4 are shell wall, and bannerWord only fills air; shell-a must leave them air, or the sign moves
Quartz jambs of tallWindow and slidingDoor are not placed: those wall cells are locked to the shells (jambs: false / frame: false used); the glazing and doors sit flush
25 floating-shutter fit issues on plots 4 and 6 (x99..106 z10, x120..131 z2..10) until shell-b builds those walls; re-run fit after the merge
BIKES banners at z0 y5 float until shell-b builds the z1 fascia; the banners need a solid block behind them
Plot 7 windows carry no shutters (they sit on the plot edge); the office lintel and the lean-to small windows from OPENINGS are not placed
Boathouse door done, but the item's steep red roof and birch frame need the roofs part; elements.md item left unticked
Arcade door x42..43 z4 opens through the arcade pier at x42, as the OPENINGS table gives it; check the render once shell-a is merged

waste.what: Worked out each OPENINGS cell by hand: window run start, face, width and the two shutter cells beside every window (front cell offset per face).
waste.cost: about 90 window and door calls typed out one by one, with coordinates computed per face
waste.tool: An OPENINGS-to-code generator: read plan.md's OPENINGS table and emit window/tallWindow/doorPair/slidingDoor calls with shutter sides computed from face and width, so the table is the single source.

waste.what: Found the locked-wall refusals (quartz jambs, 99 refused writes) only after a full build, then switched jambs off by sed.
waste.cost: two make.sh runs and one sed pass
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for runParts that lists which cells of a part would be refused against the earlier parts, before the build, or a helper option that only uses the cells the shell leaves air.

waste.what: Found plaquePlan with material null returns banners in the cell in front of the wall (z-1, outside the plot); only a plan read exposed it.
waste.cost: one failed GYM placement plus two inspection calls
waste.tool: plaque or bannerWord should refuse, or report, any cell outside the plot footprint; a plot-bound check on the sign helpers.

waste.what: Checked block contents cell by cell with a node one-liner against load() to confirm the GYM and BIKES cells.
waste.cost: three small inspection scripts
waste.tool: `mcd cells build.nbt x,y,z ...` or a `mcd fit` option that prints the block at a list of cells.

waste.what: Judged shutter and window placement by zoom renders, one image at a time, because the front elevation is too small to read at site scale.
waste.cost: three renders, two of them images read into context
waste.tool: A `mcd render --plot x0,x1` option that frames one plot at a readable scale.

companions.task: Fit the quartz jambs round every tall window and sliding door, if shell-a leaves those wall cells as air, and set the transom glazing over the bike-shop door.
Letter the GYM sign on the vestibule fascia in banner letters, once the fascia cells are left air, and check the BIKES banners sit on the z1 fascia.
Hang the green shutters on plots 4 and 6 after shell-b builds their walls, and re-check the floating-shutter list.

summary:
grounds and light: parts/grounds.mjs built: 4 door steps, lawns on open ground of plots 0,1,2,4,6-9 (open-sky test), dirt_path at plot 4 and 6, 3 trees and 2 hedges, 12 lamp posts, 3 eave lanterns, and floor/deck lanterns in every single- and two-storey mass (60 lanterns).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt: grounds line shows 962 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check reports 0 floating and fit is OK. Interiors of the built masses measure min 7-13 at y1 (W1 was 7, fixed to 8+).
Lantern refusals depend on other parts (porch roof, awning) being present at merge; plots 4-9 shells and roofs are stubs in this copy, so their lighting and lawn edges are unverified.
polish: Eave lanterns for the plot 2 porch (x73, x76 z1 y2) and plot 5 awning (x112 z0 y2) were refused in this copy because those roofs are not built yet; they should land in the merge, but unverified.
Lean-tos two cells wide have no interior to light, so they stay unlit; only plot 0 lean-to a (interior 5..6) gets a lantern.
Plot 9 boathouse (walls y1..2, roof from y3) has no headroom for a floor lantern and is unlit; plot 8 garage and plot 7 north doors have no lantern (the lintel cell is the door opening).
Two-storey upper floors (y4) are not lit; ground floors of plots 4, 6, 7 are lit only once their shells exist.
Lawns, trees and hedges on plots 4-9 are checked only against stub shells here; re-run make.sh after parts 1-5 land to confirm nothing refused and that the open-sky lawns match the walls.
Plot 5 z8 paved strip and plot 3 yard need no work beyond default smooth_stone; plot 9 lawn is two open cells only.
Trees: only plot 0 has room for a 5-wide crown; the rest of the plots are too narrow to plant without the crown hitting a wall.

waste.what: Wrote the open-sky test (no block in y1..10 above a ground cell) and the lawn loops by hand, cell by cell, to keep grass out from under the buildings.
waste.cost: about 240 lawn cells, each tested through g.get across 10 y-levels; one retry when the path cells were overwritten by lawn order
waste.tool: A footprint helper in vocab (e.g. openGround(g, rect) that returns the open cells of a rect) and a plan.json footprint map would have given lawns and paths without per-cell tests.

waste.what: Copied each mass rect from plan.md into lists in grounds.mjs and worked out interior lantern positions by hand (inset 1, spread every 6 cells, storey choice).
waste.cost: one list of 19 masses and two spread loops; no retries on coordinates
waste.tool: A lighting helper in build library: lightMasses(g, rects, { storeys }) that derives interiors, spacing and the deck/floor choice from the mass table in plan.md.

waste.what: Measured interior light by writing a rooms.json of the mass interiors and running mcd light, then deleting it, to find dark cells.
waste.cost: 2 runs and one hand-written rooms file (about 12 boxes); parsing a 156-wide ASCII map by eye
waste.tool: mcd light --masses plan.md (or a plan.json rooms list generated from the mass table) so each building's interior is measured in one call with a min/dark summary.

waste.what: Spot-checked placed blocks (steps, lawn, lantern) with a node one-liner against load().
waste.cost: three queries, one refused lantern found that way
waste.tool: mcd at build.nbt x,y,z (print block and state at a cell) and a refused-list in the part report with the block that blocked it.

waste.what: Judged the tree and lawn placement from a zoom render; the street and look sheets are too small at 156 blocks wide to read plot-level detail.
waste.cost: two renders and some ambiguity about which side of the view was west
waste.tool: mcd zoom with a labelled plot grid overlay (x and z ticks at the plot edges) so cells can be read against plan.md.

companions.task: Light the two-storey interiors on the upper floor (y4) and the boathouse, which have no headroom for standing lanterns; decide hidden light for the shopfront and the garage door.
Place trees and hedges on the narrow lawns of plots 2, 6, 7 and 8 where a 5-wide crown does not fit, or choose shrubs instead; check crowns against the walls once shells exist.
Lay the paved apron and the plot 5 z8 strip, and the plot 0 apron pattern (smooth stone slabs in a stretcher bond), without disturbing the door steps.

summary:
inspection: Fixed all 9 FIT bottom-slab issues by swapping the slab support for full blocks in two parts modules: porch post bases (plot 2, x67..82 step 3, z0) and C2 entry deck (plot 6 x123..124 z2..3, which carries C1's overhang stairs), plus the cupola's rod cap cell at 125,9,6.
make.sh rebuilt build.nbt; WALK ok (6767 cells reached, no rooms to fix); FIT now reports OK.
polish: Not in the lists, left alone: the fittings part reports REFUSED 2 writes at 153,3,0 and 154,3,0 (birch_planks already placed by the boathouse B1 gable; the fittings wanted brick_stairs there). Build is whole and both checks pass, but the refusal is still in the build log.

waste.what: Worked out which part or helper placed each floating block (the C1 eave overhang stairs at y4 sitting on the C2 deck, the porch post bases, the cupola cap under the rod) by grepping parts and vocab, since the fit line names only the cell and the block.
waste.cost: about 6 greps/reads and 3 rebuild-check cycles; the 9 issues fell to 1 new one after the first pass, which the first fix made visible
waste.tool: fit output that adds the placing part and helper (e.g. 'placed by roofs-b C2 deck' or 'cupola()') and lists every block that would be above a slab in one pass, so a fix does not expose a new one
